name: Accessory pairing without broad Bluetooth access
plain: A system picker pairs one chosen accessory so the app never needs the full Bluetooth scan.
meaning: Reduces what an app learns: it sees only the accessory the person picked, not every device nearby, so a pairing flow cannot double as a presence survey.

android.prompt_ui: System device chooser; association remains until removed
android.persistence: Until user or app removes the association
android.revocation: Settings > Connected devices; app can disassociate
android.note: Android 13 adds presence observation; Android 16 adds device presence improvements and self-managed association.

ios.prompt_ui: Apple sheet showing only matching accessories; one tap to pair
ios.note: iOS 26 expands to Wi-Fi accessories and migration of already paired devices.

limits.headline: Can pair the one accessory you pick without seeing other Bluetooth devices nearby
limits.user_action: You tap your accessory in the system pairing sheet
can: Show you a system picker listing only matching accessories
Connect to the accessory you choose with one tap
Keep the link until you remove it (Android)
cannot: Turn a pairing flow into a survey of who is around
Need the broad Bluetooth scan permission for this step
limits.differs: iPhone adds Wi-Fi accessories and migration of paired devices in iOS 26; Android adds device presence checks from Android 13 and more in 16.

story.what_it_is: A system screen that pairs one accessory you pick, so the app never gets the broad Bluetooth scan.

marketing.name: AccessorySetupKit
marketing.pitch: Pair accessories with a simple sheet that shows only the device you pick, with no broad Bluetooth access.

story.for_you: A clean picture sheet appears with your headphones or watch. You tap it and it connects. The app does not need to ask to scan for everything near you.
story.for_makers: The app maker skips a scary permission prompt and wins more trust. Setup is smoother, so fewer people give up. The platform makes sure the app sees only the one device it was given.

use_cases.example: A running watch maker pairs the band with its app without scanning every device in the park.
A pair of smart earbuds shows a photo of the case in the sheet and connects in a tap.
A smart lock app finds only the lock you are holding your phone near.
A glucose monitor or blood pressure cuff pairs without exposing other nearby devices.
A camera or drone controller app finds your device from a pretty setup screen.
A kids' smartwatch pairs with a parent's phone without the app learning about neighbours' devices.
A headset companion app pairs once and remembers the headset.

risks: Only works for apps that adopt it
story.android_note: Android has a similar companion device pairing flow. Android 13 added presence watching, and Android 16 improves it.
story.ios_note: iOS 26 extends the sheet to Wi-Fi accessories and can move already paired devices across.

technical_bounds: The app cannot scan for other accessories after pairing via the picker alone

history.change: Wi-Fi accessory support and migration APIs
